title: The Power of Lifelong Learning
outline: 开头:知识半衰期缩短,终身学习成为必需 → 中间:1)保持职业竞争力 2)滋养精神世界 3)举一个职场转型例子 → 结尾:把学习当作生活方式而非任务
content:
In an era when knowledge becomes outdated faster than ever before, learning can no longer end with a diploma. Lifelong learning has shifted from a noble choice to a practical necessity. Those who stop learning after graduation often find their skills quietly shrinking in value, while those who keep studying remain adaptable when industries transform.
The benefits of lifelong learning are both external and internal. Externally, continuous learning keeps us competitive in the job market. A marketing manager who masters data analysis, for instance, can survive a wave of automation that eliminates colleagues who refuse to change. Internally, learning nourishes the mind. Reading history, practicing a language, or studying astronomy enriches our inner world far beyond any salary.
Admittedly, lifelong learning demands time and discipline, especially for people burdened with work and family. Yet modern technology has lowered the barrier dramatically: online courses, podcasts and e-books allow anyone with a smartphone to turn fragmented time into growth.
In conclusion, lifelong learning is not a task to finish but a way to live. The moment we regard learning as a lifelong companion rather than a temporary ladder to a degree, we gain the confidence to face an uncertain future.

title: Practical Skills or Academic Knowledge?
outline: 开头:引出争论:大学应偏重实用技能还是学术知识 → 亮明观点:两者兼顾但学术为本 → 论证1:学术训练培养可迁移能力;论证2:纯技能易过时;让步:实用课程确有价值 → 结尾:重申平衡,学术为根技能为叶
content:
A heated debate is under way on campus: should universities prioritize practical skills that employers demand, or academic knowledge that builds the mind? While practical training has obvious appeal, I firmly believe that academic foundations must remain at the core of higher education.
Supporters of skill-centered education argue that graduates need to survive the job market immediately. It is true that courses in coding, writing and public speaking translate directly into offers. However, such advantages are short-lived, for specific tools change every few years. What lasts is the deeper ability that academic training cultivates: how to analyze an unfamiliar problem, weigh evidence and construct a logical argument. A philosophy graduate may not know the latest software, but she knows how to think, and software can be learned in months while thinking cannot.
Moreover, universities are not vocational schools. If they simply chase market trends, they will lose the very mission that distinguishes them from training centers.
Of course, this does not mean ignoring practice. The ideal model combines the two: rigorous theory in the classroom, internships and projects during vacations. Knowledge gives roots; skills give leaves. A university that remembers this order will serve its students for a lifetime, not merely for their first interview.

title: Surviving Information Overload
outline: 开头:描述信息过载现象及危害(焦虑/浅薄) → 原因:推送算法+收藏等于学会的错觉 → 对策:1)精选信息源 2)定时而非随时 3)以输出代替囤积 → 结尾:做信息的主人
content:
Every morning, billions of people wake up and immediately dive into an ocean of information: news feeds, group messages, short videos and endless notifications. Instead of feeling informed, many of us feel exhausted and anxious. Information overload has quietly become one of the defining burdens of modern life.
The causes are worth noticing. First, algorithms are designed to capture attention, so platforms keep pushing more content than we can possibly absorb. Second, we ourselves mistake collecting for learning. We bookmark articles we never read and save videos we never review, which creates an illusion of progress while our minds grow shallower.
To cope with this problem, three strategies are effective. To begin with, we should choose information sources deliberately, just as we choose friends. Following a few high-quality accounts beats wandering through thousands of random ones. In addition, checking news at two or three fixed moments a day, rather than refreshing every few minutes, returns hours of deep attention to us. Most importantly, we should replace hoarding with output: writing a short summary or explaining an idea to a friend turns passive input into active knowledge.
Information should serve the mind, not besiege it. Only by selecting strictly, scheduling wisely and outputting regularly can we remain masters of information instead of its servants.

title: Perseverance: The Quiet Engine of Success
outline: 开头:引用'滴水穿石'或英文谚语,点明毅力主题 → 论证1:天赋需毅力加持,例子:语言学习每天二十分钟;论证2:毅力把失败转为经验,发明/科研例子 → 让步:方向错误时需调整而非死撑 → 结尾:重申坚持+正确方向
content:
'Little by little, one goes far.' This old saying captures a truth that modern culture often forgets: behind almost every achievement stands not a burst of genius but quiet, stubborn perseverance.
Consider how talents actually grow. A brilliant memory means little in language learning if the learner practices for one intense weekend and then disappears for a month. Twenty minutes a day, repeated for years, beats any short-lived enthusiasm. The same pattern appears in science and business: most breakthroughs arrive only after countless failed attempts, and it is perseverance that converts each failure into a lesson rather than a full stop.
Admittedly, perseverance is not blind stubbornness. Continuing down a wrong path with maximum effort merely wastes time. True perseverance includes the patience to adjust methods while holding the goal steady. The sailor who cannot control the wind must learn to adjust the sails, but he never stops sailing.
For us students, the message is practical and encouraging. Do not be intimidated by the gap between your present level and your dream. Break the journey into daily steps, accept small failures as tuition, and keep walking. Success is rarely a lightning strike; it is a wall built brick by brick by those who simply refused to quit.

title: Short Videos and the Fate of Deep Reading
outline: 开头:短视频流行,深度阅读式微 → 原因分析:即时快感+碎片时间 → 危害:注意力碎片化/思辨力下降 → 让步:短视频也有价值 → 对策:固定阅读时间+以读促思 → 结尾:两者可共存但要有主次
content:
On every bus and subway, a familiar scene repeats itself: heads bowed, thumbs swiping, eyes fixed on fifteen-second videos. Meanwhile, libraries report that fewer people finish a single book a year. The rise of short videos and the decline of deep reading form one of the most striking contrasts of our time.
The shift is understandable. Short videos demand nothing from viewers; pleasure arrives instantly, requiring no patience or imagination. Deep reading, by contrast, asks us to concentrate, to visualize, to question. In an age of exhausted workers, the easier option naturally wins our leisure hours.
Yet we pay a hidden price. Reading trains the mind to follow long arguments and to sit with difficult ideas; scrolling trains it only to flick away. Studies link heavy short-video use with shrinking attention spans and weaker critical thinking. If a generation loses the habit of reading long texts, its ability to reason deeply will shrink with it.
This is not to condemn short videos, which educate and entertain millions in legitimate ways. The real question is priority. We can reclaim deep reading with small habits: twenty pages before sleep, a paper book on the commute, a weekly discussion of what we read. Screens will not disappear, but when reading regains its throne in our daily schedule, entertainment becomes a spice rather than the main course.

title: Caring for the College Mind
outline: 开头:大学生心理问题上升(数据泛化) → 原因:学业内卷/社交比较/未来焦虑 → 对策:1)学校心理服务常态化 2)规律运动与睡眠 3)敢于求助去污名化 → 结尾:心理健康与成绩同样重要
content:
Behind the lively surface of campus life, a quieter crisis is spreading: surveys across many universities indicate that a growing proportion of students report anxiety, insomnia or a persistent sense of emptiness. Caring for the college mind has become as urgent as improving grades.
Three pressures deserve attention. Academic competition has intensified, with internships, competitions and certificates crowding every semester. Social media forces students into endless comparison with the most dazzling highlights of others' lives. And an uncertain job market turns the future itself into a source of stress. Under such weight, struggling mentally is not weakness but a natural response.
Solutions must work on several levels. Universities should normalize psychological services, offering regular workshops and confidential counseling, so that visiting a counselor feels as ordinary as visiting a dentist. Students themselves can build protective routines: regular exercise, sufficient sleep and honest conversations with friends have proven effects that rival any technique. Finally, society must keep dismantling the stigma around seeking help; asking for support is an act of courage and wisdom, not a stain on a resume.
A diploma measures knowledge, but a healthy mind makes both study and life possible. Only when universities treat mental well-being as seriously as academic performance can students truly flourish.

title: Alone or Together? Rethinking Teamwork
outline: 开头:时代赞美团队,单干被低估 → 观点:合作完成大事,但独立思考是合作的前提 → 论证:1)团队优势:互补/纠错 2)风险:从众与搭便车 3)独立思考的价值 → 结尾:会独立思考的人组成团队最强
content:
Our era celebrates teamwork so enthusiastically that working alone almost sounds like a defect. Posters in offices praise collaboration, and job ads list 'team spirit' as a basic requirement. Yet the relationship between working alone and working together deserves more careful thought.
Teamwork, admittedly, achieves what individuals cannot. Complex projects demand complementary talents: a product needs designers, engineers and marketers. Teams also correct individual blindness; an idea tested by ten colleagues is far more reliable than one applauded by a single mind.
However, groups carry hidden dangers. Members may slide into conformity, silencing doubts to keep harmony, or free-ride on the efforts of others. History offers countless examples of brilliant individuals whose insights emerged precisely because they stepped away from the crowd to think independently. An idea must often be born alone before it can be refined together.
Therefore, the real skill is not choosing between the two modes but combining them. We should cultivate the discipline of independent thinking, forming our own judgment before meetings, and then bring that judgment into the team to be tested and improved. The strongest teams are not those whose members think alike, but those whose members each think for themselves and argue honestly toward a shared goal.
In short: think alone, decide together. A team of independent minds outperforms both the lone genius and the unanimous chorus.

title: The Green Shift in Everyday Life
outline: 开头:环保从口号进入日常细节 → 现象列举:出行/消费/饮食的变化 → 动力:政策+青年观念+成本下降 → 挑战:便利与习惯的阻力 → 结尾:微小选择汇聚成转变
content:
Environmental protection used to live in slogans and conferences, far from daily routine. Today it has quietly moved into our pockets, kitchens and wardrobes: shared bikes crowd the streets, reusable cups hang on backpacks, and second-hand platforms flourish among young consumers. A green shift is reshaping everyday life.
Several forces drive this change. Government policies, from plastic-bag charges to subway expansion, have made green choices cheaper and easier. Meanwhile, a generational shift is under way: many young people regard sustainable living not as sacrifice but as identity and taste. Technology plays its part too, as electric vehicles and energy-saving appliances fall rapidly in price.
The shift, however, remains fragile. Convenience still defeats good intentions when it rains and the bike lane floods, when delivery arrives wrapped in three layers of plastic. Habits built on low prices and speed do not dissolve overnight, and green options must compete on experience, not merely on conscience.
Even so, the direction is clear. Every reusable bag and every short-video about zero-waste living normalizes a different way of life. Individual choices seem tiny, yet multiplied by hundreds of millions of consumers, they push markets and policies forward. The green shift teaches a larger lesson about social change: it rarely begins with a revolution; it begins with ordinary people quietly choosing differently, day after day.

title: AI Tutors Enter the Classroom
outline: 开头:AI学习工具迅速普及的现象 → 现象两面:个性化辅导/答疑 vs 抄袭依赖与思维惰性 → 深层:工具放大使用者的学习态度 → 结尾:善用者借力,滥用者受害
content:
Walk into any university library and you will see students chatting quietly, not with each other, but with artificial intelligence. AI tutors that explain calculus at midnight, correct essays in seconds and quiz users on demand have moved from science fiction into daily study routines. Education, arguably the last craft industry, is being reshaped at remarkable speed.
The promise is genuine. An AI tutor never tires, never mocks a silly question, and adjusts its pace to each learner, which is a blessing for students who cannot afford private coaching. Yet the same convenience carries a hidden cost. When answers arrive before questions are fully formed, thinking can quietly atrophy. Some students now outsource not only reference checks but the very act of reasoning.
The deeper truth is that such tools amplify the attitude of the user rather than replace it. For a learner who treats AI as a patient teacher and checks its answers critically, it widens access to knowledge. For one who treats it as a homework machine, it merely automates the avoidance of learning.
AI in the classroom is neither savior nor villain; it is a mirror. Schools should teach not only how to use these tools but when not to, and students should remember that the point of education was never to produce answers quickly, but to build minds that can question them.

title: The Rise of Second-Hand Chic
outline: 开头:二手交易从小众走向潮流 → 原因:1)环保意识 2)经济理性 3)寻宝乐趣与个性表达 → 隐忧:卫生/真假/炒作 → 结尾:消费观念的成熟标志
content:
Not long ago, buying second-hand goods carried a faint smell of embarrassment, something people hid from their neighbors. Today the reverse is true: vintage jackets, refurbished phones and pre-loved books are proudly displayed on social media, and second-hand platforms are among the fastest-growing apps on the market. Thrift has turned into chic.
Three forces explain the trend. Environmental awareness leads the way, as young consumers increasingly feel uncomfortable adding to mountains of textile and electronic waste. Economic rationality follows: with prices of new goods climbing, a half-priced, hardly-used alternative simply makes sense. Finally, there is the pleasure of the hunt. Unlike standardized new products, second-hand markets offer surprise, story and individuality, letting buyers assemble a style no advertisement can package.
The trend is not without problems. Hygiene standards are vague, fake antiques and counterfeit sneakers fool eager buyers, and some resellers hoard scarce items to inflate prices, betraying the sharing spirit the market celebrates.
Yet these are growing pains rather than fatal flaws. Platforms are building inspection and certification services, and regulation is catching up. What matters more is the shift in mindset underneath: value is being redefined from shiny and new to useful and loved. When a generation proudly wears what someone else no longer needs, consumption is finally growing up.

title: Grades Are Not the Whole Picture
outline: 开头:分数崇拜现象,家长学生以分数论英雄 → 亮明观点:分数重要但只是能力的一部分 → 论证1:分数衡量范围有限;论证2:用人单位更看综合素养;论证3:唯分数伤害身心健康与好奇心 → 让步:考试仍是最公平的尺子之一 → 结尾:重视分数,不被分数奴役
content:
In countless families, one question decides the mood of an entire semester: what did you score? Grades have become the currency of self-worth for students and the measure of parenting for adults. Respect them as we may, grades are not, and should never be, the whole picture of a person.
A score is a snapshot of narrow performance under strict conditions. It rewards certain kinds of memory, speed and test-taking skill, while remaining silent about creativity, resilience, empathy and the ability to cooperate, qualities that decide far more of our lives than any exam does. Employers consistently report that they hire for attitude and train for skill; no transcript lists those.
The costs of grade worship are also visible. Students optimize for testable knowledge and abandon curiosity for anything unexamined; anxiety and burnout spread from top schools to ordinary classrooms; and the fear of failure teaches young people to avoid challenges precisely when they should be embracing them.
Admittedly, examinations remain among the fairest instruments society has for selection, and dismissing grades entirely would be naive. Hard work should show its results. But a ruler is only trustworthy within its range. Let grades tell us what they truly measure, and let character, health and genuine interest occupy their rightful place in the report card of a life. Score the exam, but never let the exam score you.

title: Should City Centers Ban Private Cars?
outline: 开头:拥堵与污染引出限行争议 → 反方:限行损害自由与商圈,穷人负担重 → 正方:公交改善先行,限行是最后一步;健康与效率收益巨大 → 提出折中:拥堵收费+新能源豁免+公交升级 → 结尾:支持的立场,渐进实施
content:
Rush hour in a modern city center is a parking lot with delusions of movement. As congestion chokes streets and exhaust fumes choke lungs, many cities are debating a radical prescription: banning private cars from downtown areas. The idea offends many drivers, yet on balance, I believe carefully designed restrictions deserve support.
The objections deserve a hearing. A car represents freedom and convenience, and for parents, the elderly and people with disabilities it is often a necessity rather than a luxury. Merchants also fear that fewer cars mean fewer customers. Such concerns explain why bans announced without alternatives breed anger instead of clean air.
However, the evidence from cities that have acted is encouraging. When downtown Oslo and Madrid restricted cars, shops did not die; foot traffic and business rose, noise fell, and streets once reserved for metal became space for cafes and children. Public health researchers found measurable drops in air pollution within months. Crucially, successful cities phased in the change: they first upgraded buses, subways and cycling lanes, then charged or restricted private cars, and always kept exemptions for those with genuine needs.
A total, sudden ban would indeed be unjust. But the choice is never between unlimited cars and no cars. Congestion pricing, license-plate rules, low-emission zones and reliable public transport can be combined and adjusted. The destination is a city center that belongs to people rather than to parking, and the sooner we drive toward it, the better.

title: Easing the Loneliness of the Elderly
outline: 开头:老龄化+独居老人孤独成为社会问题 → 原因:家庭结构变化/数字鸿沟/社区功能弱化 → 对策:1)社区互助与老年活动中心 2)数字适老培训 3)代际共居与志愿探访 → 结尾:孤独问题的答案在人与人的连接
content:
In rapidly aging societies, a quiet epidemic is spreading that no medicine can cure: loneliness among the elderly. Behind millions of closed doors, older people who once anchored large families now spend entire days without a single conversation. Solving this problem is becoming as important as funding pensions.
The causes are structural. Urbanization scatters children across cities and countries, leaving parents in empty nests. Communities that once organized life around courtyards and neighborhoods have dissolved into apartment blocks of strangers. Meanwhile, services from banking to healthcare have moved online, building a digital wall that many seniors cannot climb.
Yet the remedies are within reach when society decides to act. Community centers that offer meals, classes and simple companionship transform isolated flats into social worlds; regular volunteer visits give homebound seniors both practical help and a reason to dress up. Digital literacy courses, taught patiently by young volunteers, turn the smartphone from a source of fear into a window to grandchildren. More ambitious still, intergenerational programs that connect retirement homes with schools and cheap student housing inside senior communities benefit both sides: the young gain affordable living and wisdom; the old gain noise, energy and purpose.
Technology and policy both have roles to play, but the heart of the answer is ancient and simple: people need people. A society is measured by how it treats those who can no longer give anything except gratitude and stories, and those two gifts are worth more than we think.

title: Waste Not: Fixing the Food Waste Problem
outline: 开头:从田头到餐桌的浪费触目惊心(约三分之一) → 危害:资源环境+伦理 → 对策:1)消费者:按需采购+光盘 2)商家:动态折扣与捐赠机制 3)技术:保质期标签改革与食物银行 → 结尾:节约是系统性工程
content:
Roughly one third of all food produced on Earth never reaches a human stomach. It rots in fields, expires on supermarket shelves and ends up scraped from plates into bins. In a world where millions still go hungry, such waste is not merely inefficient; it is morally difficult to defend.
The scale of the problem hides in its scattered nature: everyone wastes a little, so nobody feels responsible. Yet multiplied by billions of households, leftovers become a monster that devours water, land, fuel and labor, and then decomposes into methane, a greenhouse gas far more potent than carbon dioxide.
The fixes exist at every level of the chain. For households, the weapons are unglamorous but effective: shopping with a list, understanding the difference between best-before and unsafe-after, and treating leftovers as ingredients rather than garbage. Restaurants can offer smaller portions and doggy bags without shame. Supermarkets can sell near-expiry goods at dynamic discounts and donate unsold food through food banks instead of locking bins. Governments can standardize date labels and set reduction targets, as several European countries have done with encouraging results.
What is ultimately required is a change of attitude: from treating food as a cheap commodity to treating it as embedded labor, water and life. A culture that wastes a third of its meals has not yet finished learning gratitude. Waste not, want not, as the old saying goes, is not a slogan but a system, and every meal is a chance to vote for it.

title: On Humility: The Vessel That Holds More
outline: 开头:引'满招损,谦受益'英文表述 → 论证1:谦逊是学习的前提(空杯心态);论证2:谦逊赢得合作与信任(领导力例子);对比:傲慢的代价 → 澄清:谦逊≠自我贬低,而是准确评估自己 → 结尾:重申谦逊是强者姿态
content:
'Fullness invites loss; modesty brings gain.' This ancient Chinese maxim expresses a truth that modern psychology keeps rediscovering: humility is not weakness but the vessel that holds the most.
Humility is, first of all, the precondition of learning. A cup that is already full accepts nothing more. The student who believes he already understands stops listening; the professional who is certain of her method stops updating it. In fast-changing fields, yesterday's certainty is today's error, and the humble habit of saying 'I might be wrong' is precisely what keeps knowledge flowing in.
Humility also builds the trust on which cooperation depends. Colleagues forgive a leader who admits mistakes; they quietly sabotage one who claims infallibility. The most respected experts are often those who say 'I don't know, but I will find out', because such honesty makes everything else they say credible.
Humility must not be confused with self-erasure. It is not thinking less of yourself, but thinking of yourself less accurately and less often, evaluating your strengths and limits calmly, without swagger or shame. Arrogance, by contrast, is not confidence but a fear of exposure, loud precisely where it is hollow.
In an age of self-promotion, choosing humility looks like a disadvantage. It is in fact a long-term strategy: the arrogant protect their image and stop growing, while the humble protect their learning and keep growing. The full cup spills; the empty one is still being filled.

title: Reading Versus Doing: Knowledge Needs a Body
outline: 开头:引'纸上得来终觉浅,绝知此事要躬行' → 论证1:书本知识的抽象性与实践的具体性(学游泳例子);论证2:实践反馈修正认知,动手产生真问题 → 让步:没有理论的实践是盲目试错 → 结尾:知行合一,以行验知
content:
'Knowledge from books is always shallow; to truly understand, you must practice it yourself.' Written a thousand years ago, this line from a Song dynasty poet anticipates a debate that every learner still faces today: what books give us, and what only action can teach.
Books compress the experience of others into portable form, which is precisely their power and their limit. You can memorize every manual on swimming, yet the first time your face enters the water, panic does not read footnotes. Abstract knowledge omits the details that matter: the weight of the clay on the wheel, the timing of a negotiation, the fatigue in your legs. Practice restores those details, and with them, understanding.
Doing does more than complete theory; it corrects it. Hands-on work generates feedback that no page can predict, and feedback generates the sharpest questions. Many breakthroughs in science and engineering began when someone in the field noticed that the textbook did not match the workshop. Reading without doing, therefore, tends to produce confident opinions; doing without reading produces scars, but also truth.
This is not an argument against study. Action without knowledge is blind trial and error, endlessly repeating what others have already solved. The ideal is the loop the old poet implied: read, act, reflect, read again. Let every chapter be tested against reality, and every failure send you back to the book, wiser. Knowledge needs a body; give yours to what you learn.

title: Do What Is Worth Doing (2020.9真题)
outline: 开头:引述「做值得做的事」并指出现代人困于忙碌却鲜有值得 → 中间:1)值得之事多带延迟满足(学一门硬技能、养一段关系);2)社会用「忙」奖励表演,用「成果」奖励深耕 → 结尾:每晚问自己「今天做的事,一年后是否还在」,把精力从「显得有用」转向「真正有用」。
content:
An old saying goes, "It is better to do one thing worth doing than a hundred things merely done." Modern life, however, seems engineered to test exactly this principle: calendars overflow, notifications never stop, and yet at the end of a exhausting week, few of us can name a single task that truly mattered.
The reason is that worth is rarely urgent. Answering emails feels productive because the feedback is instant; learning a difficult skill or rebuilding a strained relationship pays off only months later, and nothing on the screen applauds the effort. We are, in effect, rewarded for looking busy long before we are rewarded for being useful.
The remedy is a small nightly question: of everything I did today, what will still matter in a year? Asked honestly and repeatedly, it quietly reorders a life. Busyness becomes a tool rather than a trophy, and the hours we have—never as many as we imagine—finally go to things that deserve them.

title: Chart: China's Urbanisation Rate (2021.6真题)
outline: 图表描述:柱状图显示中国常住人口城镇化率从1980年的约20%升至2020年的60%以上 → 分析原因:工业化与服务业集聚、户籍与土地政策改革、基础设施大规模投入 → 评论:成就背后关注城市病与新市民融入,未来城镇化重在质量。
content:
The bar chart illustrates a remarkable social transformation: China's urbanisation rate climbed from roughly twenty percent in 1980 to over sixty percent in 2020, meaning the country urbanised in four decades what took Europe more than a century.
Three forces drove this shift. First, industrialisation concentrated jobs in cities, pulling rural labour into factories and service sectors. Second, policy reforms—from the household registration system to land markets—lowered the barriers to moving and settling. Third, massive infrastructure investment made urban life on this scale physically possible: metro systems, housing blocks and power grids built at unprecedented speed.
The achievement is undeniable, yet the chart also points to challenges. Rapid urbanisation has brought congestion, housing pressure and the difficult integration of migrant populations. The next stage, as policymakers now emphasise, is less about how fast cities grow than about how well they serve the people already living in them. Urbanisation, ultimately, is measured not in percentages but in quality of life.

title: Chart: The Expansion of Higher Education (2021.6真题)
outline: 图表描述:中国高等教育在校生规模与毛入学率数十年持续上升,2020年前后毛入学率突破50%进入普及化阶段 → 原因:高校扩招政策、经济发展带来的教育投入、家庭对教育的重视 → 评论:从精英化到普及化,关注质量、结构与就业匹配。
content:
The chart displays the steady expansion of China's higher education: gross enrolment rose from the low single digits decades ago to surpass fifty percent, moving the system from elite to universal stage, with enrolment figures now the largest in the world.
Several factors account for this growth. Sustained economic development provided the funding for campuses, faculty and research. Policy decisions to expand enrolment widened access for millions of families who had previously seen university as unreachable. And a deep cultural respect for education ensured that demand never wavered, even as supply multiplied.
Universal access, however, brings new questions. As graduate numbers grow, the value of a degree alone declines, and employers increasingly look for skills that classrooms do not automatically confer. The challenge for the next decade is therefore less about enrolling more students than about teaching them better—shifting from scale to substance, and from credentials to competence.

title: Chart: China's Poverty Reduction (2021.6真题)
outline: 图表描述:按现行标准,中国农村贫困人口从2012年底的约9899万减少到2020年全部脱贫,贫困发生率从10.2%降至0 → 分析:精准扶贫方略、产业扶贫与易地搬迁、基础设施与公共服务投入 → 评论:减贫奇迹的启示与防止返贫的长期任务。
content:
The chart records one of the most rapid poverty reductions in history: according to current standards, China's rural poor population fell from nearly one hundred million in 2012 to zero in 2020, with the poverty incidence dropping from over ten percent to nil.
This outcome was not automatic. A targeted poverty-alleviation strategy directed resources to specific villages and households rather than spreading funds thinly. Industry support and relocation programmes gave impoverished regions the means to earn rather than merely receive, while investment in roads, power, schools and clinics removed the structural barriers that had kept poverty self-perpetuating.
The lesson extends beyond China: large-scale poverty reduction is possible when policy is precise, sustained and matched by infrastructure. Yet the chart marks an ending and a beginning at once. With absolute poverty eliminated, the task shifts to preventing relapse—consolidating gains, supporting fragile households, and ensuring that growth continues to reach those it has reached last.

title: Chart: The Rise of New Energy Vehicles (仿真)
outline: 图表描述:中国新能源汽车年销量从2016年的约50万辆增长到2023年的近950万辆,占新车销售比重超过30% → 原因:政策支持(补贴、牌照、免税)、技术进步(电池成本下降、续航提升)、消费观念转变 → 评论:产业领先伴随充电设施、电池回收与国际竞争等新课题。
content:
The chart shows new energy vehicle sales in China surging from around five hundred thousand in 2016 to nearly nine and a half million in 2023, with such vehicles now accounting for over thirty percent of all new car sales.
Three engines powered this growth. Generous policy support—purchase subsidies, tax exemptions and priority licence access—lowered the cost of switching. Rapid advances in battery technology cut prices and extended range, removing the two doubts that once deterred buyers. Meanwhile, environmental awareness among young consumers turned a practical choice into a fashionable one.
China's NEV industry now leads the world, but leadership brings its own agenda: charging infrastructure in rural areas, recycling of retired batteries, and intensifying competition in overseas markets. The chart, in other words, captures not a finish line but a transition—from policy-driven beginnings to a market that must now stand on its own.

title: The Chinese Dream and the Responsibility of Youth (2025真题)
outline: 开头:中国梦不是抽象口号,而是由一代代青年的具体选择构成 → 中间:1)青年责任体现在专业深耕(科研、工匠、基层);2)体现在把个人理想与国家需求结合(乡村振兴、科技自立);3)责任不是牺牲,而是把「小我」放进「大我」后获得的格局与舞台 → 结尾:呼应开头,中国梦为青年提供可能,青年为中国梦提供答案。
content:
The Chinese Dream is often spoken of as a national vision, yet its most honest translation is personal: it is the sum of millions of young people deciding what to do with their one life.
Youth responsibility begins with depth. Whether in a laboratory debugging a chip, on a construction site perfecting a bridge, or in a village school teaching thirty children, the young contribute most when they refuse to treat their work as merely a job. It continues with direction: when personal ambition aligns with genuine social need—rural revitalisation, technological self-reliance, cultural confidence—individual effort acquires a leverage it could never achieve alone. What is often missed is that responsibility is not sacrifice. The young person who thinks beyond the self does not lose a life; they gain a stage.
Every generation inherits a country and leaves it changed. Ours is fortunate to inherit one full of possibility, and our answer to it will be written not in declarations, but in the ordinary excellence of what we choose to build.

title: Creativity in the Age of AI (2025.6真题)
outline: 开头:AI 工具普及,「一键生成」让产出变易,创意反而面临同质化危机 → 中间:1)独立思考减少:用 AI 代劳错过分析、组织、试错的思维训练;2)创意同质化:标准化答案挤占独特视角;3)即时结果消磨深度思考所需的耐心 → 结尾:AI 应是副驾驶而非代笔,先有自己的想法,再让工具放大它。
content:
As AI tools become increasingly popular, over-dependence on them is harming human creativity in critical ways. The problem stems less from the technology itself than from how easily it lets us skip the very process that makes thinking creative.
First, relying on AI to draft, plan or decide means missing the training that struggle provides. A student who lets a model organise an essay never practises organising ideas; a designer who accepts the first generated concept never argues with their own taste. Second, AI tends to average—its outputs converge toward what is most statistically expected—while creativity, by definition, thrives on what is unexpected. Third, instant answers erode the patience that original work demands; creativity has always been a slow argument with uncertainty.
The solution is not rejection but sequence: think first, then consult. Used this way, AI becomes an amplifier of ideas we already own rather than a replacement for having them. The tool can draft faster than we can; only we can decide what is worth drafting.

title: Using Social Media Responsibly (2025.6真题)
outline: 开头:社交媒体深度融入生活,「合理且负责任地使用」成为必修课 → 中间:1)隐私边界:不晒敏感信息,防患未然;2)时间管理:抵制无限下滑的信息流,学生尤需防沉迷;3)文明表达:理性讨论取代人身攻击,拒绝网络霸凌 → 结尾:负责任使用的本质是「审慎」——做工具的主人,而非算法的素材。
content:
As social media is used more and more extensively, there is a growing awareness of the importance of using it properly and responsibly. The platform itself is neutral; what matters is whether the user is awake.
Responsible use begins with privacy. Home addresses, financial details and real-time locations are not content but vulnerabilities, and the discipline of thinking twice before posting is the cheapest insurance available. It continues with time. Infinite feeds are engineered to defeat intention, and students—whose attention is their most valuable asset—need hard boundaries such as fixed checking windows and phone-free study hours. It also requires civility: behind every avatar is a person, and the gap between debate and abuse is crossed one comment at a time.
To use social media responsibly is, in the end, to remain a mindful user. Protect your data, guard your hours, and keep your words humane—then the network serves your life instead of consuming it.

title: Preparing for Tomorrow's Career (2025.6真题)
outline: 开头:求职门槛水涨船高,「毕业即胜任」已成过去,职业准备必须前置 → 中间:1)深耕专业:核心课程+实验项目,把理论变成动手能力;2)可迁移技能:实习与社团中练沟通、协作与解决问题;3)前瞻视野:跟踪行业趋势,主动学习 AI 等新工具 → 结尾:职业准备 = 学术基础 + 实践能力 + 市场认知,三者的平衡决定起点的高度。
content:
As the requirements of job applications keep rising, students ought to be better prepared for their future careers—and preparation, it turns out, is a skill that can be designed rather than hoped for.
The first element is professional depth. Whatever the major, mastery of core knowledge, tested through projects and experiments, is what separates candidates who can be trained from those already useful. The second is transferable ability. Communication, teamwork and problem-solving, sharpened in internships and student organisations, travel across every industry and every job title. The third is foresight: following industry trends, learning the tools—especially AI tools—that are reshaping every field, and adjusting one's skill set before the market demands it.
None of these can be built in the final semester. Career preparation is a four-year project, and the students who begin it early do not simply find better first jobs—they spend their whole lives one step ahead of change.
